full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that the suit land appertaining to plot No. 20 of D.S. Khatian No. 17, S.A. Khatian No. 43 originally belonged to Sheikh Nimai and Ayenuddin in equal shares. That this suit plot No. 20 contained total 18 decimals of land and each of the two original owners got 9 decimals of land in their share. Ayenuddin died leaving One son Abdul Hamid and two daughters Tomarjan Bibi and Pearjan Bibi. Later on Abdul Hamid died leaving six sons-Azhar Ali, Asoruddin, Naser, Asalat, Khejmat and Ajmat and one daughter. That the D.S. and S.A. Khatian of the suit land was correctly prepared in the name of the original owners and their successors. The plaintiffs father Md. Safizuddin purchased the share of Azhar Ali by registered kabala dated 21.08.1980. Subsequently Safiuddin gifted that land to the plaintiff by registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 08.11.1990. Thereafter Asalat and another son of Abdul Hamid sold 06/16 decimals of land to Md. Ekhlas Khan, Md. Chand Khan, Motaleb Khan and Abdus Samad Khan by registered deed dated 04.12.1980. Subsequently the plaintiff purchased that land from these purchasers by registered kabala deed dated 09.03.1988. Thus the plaintiff by way of heba-bil-ewaj deed and by purchase acquired total 7/8 decimals of land in the suit plot. The plaintiff has mutated his name and a separate khatian No. 43/1 was prepared in his name. He paid rent also to the Government upto 1405 B.S. The plain-tiff mortgaged his land to the local Agrani Bank, Dharla Branch and took loan of Tk.2,00,000/- and by spending Tk.3,00,000/- he has established two tailoring shops in his suit land and he has been continuing his tailoring business there. Due to the construction of new bridge on the river Buriganga the suit land has become very much valuable. On 14.12.2002 the plaintiff went to the local land office to pay the land development tax and came to know that this land has been recorded in the name of the government in khas khatian as plot Nos. 227, 228 and 229. The local land office refused to accept rent from the plaintiff and thus the plaintiff has been compelled to file the suit. 

 9. Mr. Rajik-Al-Jalil, the learned Deputy Attorney General has argued mainly to the effect that the suit land is within the periphery of Dharla Hat and as such it has vested upon the Government as per section 2(2) of the Hats and Bazars Ordinance. On the other hand Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin has submitted to the effect that the suit land was never within the periphery of Dharla Hat and that it was not also recorded in any of the records of right as hat and bazar and as such there was no reason for recording this land in the khas khatian of the Government. 

 11. Admittedly the suit land was tenanted land and it was recorded both in C.S. khatian and S.A. khatian in the name of original tenants. After acquiring the suit land from, the successors of the original recorded tenants by registered deeds the plaintiff mutated the suit land in his name and a separate khatian also has been prepared in his name. The plaintiff also paid rent and the Government accepted rents from the plaintiff upto 1405 B.S. It appears that both the trial court and the appellate court have considered all these facts and rightly found that the suit land was not within the periphery of Dharla Hat and there was no reason for recording the suit land in the khas khatian of the Government. The High Court Division rightly observed also that if the Government now intends to establish any hat in the suit land or include the suit land within the periphery of Dharla Hat, the Government will have to acquire the suit land in accordance with law on payment of proper consideration money to the plaintiff; that since the Government did not acquire the suit land in accordance with law the Government cannot claim any right, title or interest in the suit land and in the circumstances the recording of the suit land in the khas khatian of the Government has been wrong.
